A circular ripple spreads on the surface of a pond in a circular shape. The area of the ripple is increasing at a rate of $6\pi \,{\text{ft}}^{2}\,/\text{s}.$ How fast is the radius of the ripple increasing at the moment when the radius is $4\,\text{ft}?$ Do not round the answer.

The radius of the ripple is increasing at a rate of
{{field-1}}
$\text{ft}/\text{s}.$
worked_solution:
In this situation, we want to find $\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t}$ at the moment when $r=4,$ and we are also told that $\frac{\text{d}A}{\text{d}t}=6\pi .$

To start, let's write down the area formula for the circle and then differentiate it using implicit differentiation. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\pi {r}^{2} \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(A) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\pi {r}^{2}) \\ \frac{\text{d}A}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}r}(\pi {r}^{2}) \\ \frac{\text{d}A}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t}\cdot 2\pi r.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we substitute the given information $\frac{\text{d}A}{\text{d}t}=6\pi $ and $r=4,$ and solve for $\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t}.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}6\pi  & =\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t}\cdot 2\pi (4) \\ 6\pi  & =\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t}\cdot 8\pi  \\ \frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{3}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

We conclude that the radius is increasing at a rate of $\frac{3}{4}\,\text{ft}/\text{s}.$
